All,

I have a latent variable model where the observable are assumed conditionally independent Poisson (see the code bellow). Stan produces the following error when I run the code code below
######
Error : Error in function stan::prob::poisson_log(i): Random variable is -2147483648, but must be >= 0!
In addition: Warning message:
In storage.mode(x) <- "integer" : NAs introduced by coercion
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done
######

Thanks!

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] I am not sure what is going on
parts:
What rstan version are you using? I do not think it is 1.2.0.  

There is an issue for RStan here even for 1.2.0.  When I tried the code, the maximum of Y is:

> max(Y)
[1] 84967512093

And the error I would have is
fit <- stan(model_code = Bcca_mod, data = bcca_datn, thin=1, iter = n.samp, chains =3 , pars=c("A","B","sig_te","sig_lb","mux","muy"))

TRANSLATING MODEL 'Bcca_mod' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'Bcca_mod' NOW.
Error : int variable contained non-int values; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=Y; base type=int
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

The problem here is the maximum integer that can be represented in R is 
> .Machine$integer.max
[1] 2147483647

which is less than the above max(Y).  So when rstan preprocess the data, Y would be passed to Stan as double (real) and that is why the above error for rstan 1.2.0 happened.  For previous version of rstan, Y would be converted into integers even NA is created sometimes, which would cause sampling problem later (the reported problem here might be due to the NA's created in Y during preprocessing.)

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] I am not sure what is going on
parts:
Stan internally uses int (32 bit on most platforms)
rather than long (64 bit on most platforms), so even using
it from the command line isn't going to work (though on
Microsoft 64-bit platforms, int might be 64 bit, so
it should work there).

We could change our integer type to long. We should
probably fix the size across platform one way or the
other. Not much thought went into making them int other
than long. I didn't think anyone would use models with
int values above 2 billion.

Something that would work is to convert the integers
to real and then code up whatever distribution you
want directly using lp__.

So instead of

int<lower=0> y[N];
...
y[n] ~ poisson(lambda);

use

real<lower=0> y[N];
...
lp__ <- lp__ + y[n] * log(lambda) - lgamma(y[n] + 1) - lambda;


This is just the expression for log poisson(y[n]|lambda) using
the fact that lgamma(x+1) = log(x!) if x is an integer. In fact,
you can just drop the lgamma term because it's a constant (y[n] has
to be data because Stan doesn't support integer params).

This won't be as fast as our vectorized implementation of
Poisson -- you'd have to unfold the vectorizations for that -- but
it should work.

Should we support Poisson with a double variate?

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: y ~ Poisson(lambda) with y > 2^32
parts:
The other thing you can do is rescale all of the ints.

I'm not sure how to do that in R so that the result is
still an integer which can be passed to Stan.

You probably don't want to be fitting Poissons
with means in the billions. Even though adaptation is
exponential, it'll take Stan a while to adapt to a scale
that large during warmup.

- Bob
